subject: Confidential: People motion plan & sync on performance review timing
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Harper Langston <harper@orgdesign.co>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Confidential: People motion plan & sync on performance review timing

Team —

I wanted to share a confidential proposal for a small people motion that I think will help with coverage on Platform runtime and also align performance review cycles. High level: move 2 senior engineers (currently on Runtime Core) into a short-term Platform delivery pod for Q4 -> Q1 (6 months), with formal reporting staying with Runtime but dotted-line to Platform lead for day-to-day work. After the window we re-evaluate headcount and scope.

Why now:
- Platform has an urgent set of infra rollouts tied to Dedicated capacity that require deep runtime experience for short bursts.
- We have a set of mid-year review items that don't align with team leads' availability; syncing reviews with the people motion reduces review fatigue.

What I'm proposing (confidential):
1) Identify two volunteers (or reassign with agreement) from Runtime senior ICs (likely candidates: A and B) to join Platform pod for 6 months starting Nov 9.
2) Keep salary/job titles unchanged; reporting matrix: Runtime manager remains primary, Platform lead gets dotted-line for delivery.
3) People Ops (Priya) to brief on timing for performance reviews: decouple immediate promotion/comp cycles until after Jan calibration to avoid bias from temporary assignment.
4) Draft comms: a private note to affected ICs + manager discussion this week; broader team announcement only after blocks are in place.

Attachments: org_chart_v2.pdf (proposed matrix), confidential_role_matrix.xlsx (sensitive).

Questions for this thread:
- Legal/comp concerns? (Marissa, Priya)
- Manager bandwidth and acceptance (Laura, Markus)
- How to present this in upcoming review calibration (Priya)

I asked Harper to review the communication approach (cc'd). This is sensitive — please do not forward.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Harper Langston <harper@orgdesign.co>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Confidential: People motion plan & sync on performance review timing

Diego —

Thanks for the clear write-up. I support the idea in principle but a few concerns before we proceed:

1) Manager load: Runtime managers are already stretched for Q4 deliverables. If we keep primary reporting with Runtime, we need a clear 1:1 check-in cadence so managers don't lose sight of development plans.
2) Career/comp implications: We should be explicit that the assignment is temporary and outline how promotion/leveling signals will be handled (avoid surprises during calibration).
3) Opt-in vs. reassignment: prefer volunteers first, but we should have a fallback process if no volunteers step forward. That fallback needs HR/legal sign-off.

Suggested edits to the comms:
- Initial manager-only sync (30m) this week.
- Private 1:1 with interested ICs to cover impact to 1:1s, performance goals, and compensation expectations.
- A short FAQ for the broader team that addresses career trajectory & review timing.

I added a quick note to the attached org chart with manager bandwidth scores. Happy to run this with Markus and Priya.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Platform Product
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Harper Langston <harper@orgdesign.co>, Morgan Pierce <morgan.pierce@lawpartners.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Confidential: People motion plan & sync on performance review timing

Quick HR/legal flags (keeping this high level):

- Performance reviews: We can decouple promotion/comp cycles for the two impacted ICs, but we need explicit documentation in their review packet that notes the temporary assignment and who to route calibration questions to. Without documentation, calibration committees may interpret role change as a de facto promotion.
- PIP/risk: If any of the candidates are currently on a PIP or near-term formal performance improvement discussion, we should not move them into a temporary assignment without a documented plan. I've attached a redacted PIP_template_redacted.docx for the managers to use if needed.
- Employment terms: if we decide reassignment (non-voluntary), we need legal signoff on communication and severance language if voluntary exit is part of the fallback. Morgan (cc) — please review the two fallback phrasing options and advise.

Operational asks for Priya/People Ops:
1) Draft private manager talking points + FAQ by Thu EOD.
2) Run a short intake to capture volunteers by next Tue (Nov 2).
3) Prepare calibration placeholder notes for the review packet.

I can take point on 1 and 2 with Marissa.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Manager, People Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Confidential: People motion plan & sync on performance review timing

Diego / all —

I appreciate the heads-up. Operational notes from me:

- Candidate selection: I have two plausible volunteers in mind but want to run a private 1:1 before committing. Markus A is mid-level-senior and very interested in cross-team work; Patricia (senior) is cautious about losing runway for her IC laddering.
- Coverage plan: If both move, I'll propose a temp contractor hire (6-8 weeks) to handle the lower-skill backlog and free the remaining Runtime team to handle critical tickets. Budget for contractor is ~$30k (one-off).
- Review cadence: agree with Laura — we should keep weekly checkpoints with the Runtime managers and run a joint triage call for the first 6 weeks.

If Priya can populate the manager talking points today, I'll start scheduling 1:1s and identify volunteers.

-MK
Markus Klein
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Confidential: People motion plan & sync on performance review timing — Decisions & next steps

Team —

Thanks for the quick input. Summary and concrete next steps (confidential):

Decisions:
- We will pursue volunteer-based assignments first. Markus will complete private 1:1s and surface two volunteers by Tue (Nov 3).
- People Ops (Priya + Marissa) will publish manager talking points and an FAQ by Thu (Oct 29) — (Priya, please confirm if the date should be Tue instead).
- No promotion decisions will be made until Jan calibration; review packets will include placeholder notes about temporary assignment.
- If no volunteers emerge, escalate to Legal for fallback phrasing and options. Morgan, please prepare fallback language options by EOD Wed.
- Budget for contractor backfill approved up to $30k (Markus to own procurement).

Action items and owners:
- Markus: run 1:1s and send volunteers list (Due: 2026-11-03).
- Priya: manager talking points + FAQ + volunteer intake form (Due: 2026-11-02).
- Marissa: coordinate with Legal for fallback verbiage (Due: 2026-11-04).
- Harper: review draft comms and FAQ; return notes (Due: 2026-11-02).

Please treat as confidential. I'll post a sanitized comms package for wider distribution once volunteers are confirmed.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Director, Runtime Engineering
